thread:
alex: FYI — seeing a burst of pod evictions on gpu-prod-eu-west-1 since ~09:05 UTC. kubelet marking nodes NetworkUnavailable and evicting GPU pods. No obvious NIC link flaps in dmesg. Anyone else?
ness: yep, started ~09:05. Affected: gpu-nodeset-4a/4b/4c. Eviction reason reported as 'NetworkUnavailable' / NodeLostConnectivity.
deploy-bot: Incident created #INC-2026-302: node-evictions-east-west-latency. Assigned: @alex
alex: Pasting a few items: `kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpu-nodeset-4a`
```
NAME               STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION
gpu-nodeset-4a     Ready    gpu      42d   v1.26.3
```
But `kubectl describe node gpu-nodeset-4a` shows `NetworkUnavailable: True` and kubelet logs show repeated timeouts to 10.2.0.1:10250.
cheng: Can you paste kubelet healthcheck log lines? I suspect XDP/eBPF is dropping the health probes, especially with dual-stack IPv6 enabled.
alex: kubelet snippet:
```
I0412 09:08:12.123 kubelet.go:123] Network plugin re-check failed: dial tcp 10.2.0.1:10250: i/o timeout
I0412 09:08:12.123 network.go:78] probe response lost: xdp_tx_drops=120 rx_errors=0
```
Also ran `tc -s qdisc` which shows negligible qdisc drops, but `bpftool prog` and XDP stats show XDP_TX_DROP=180 on eno1.
marcos: We're running a custom eBPF XDP program on that subnet since Tue for L7 filtering. Could be the fall-through rule is catching kubelet probe TCP handshakes. There's a kernel change that affects IPv6 fragmented headers + XDP.
lina: @marcos which eBPF stack? Cilium or custom? If it's custom we might be accidentally matching host-origin traffic because kubelet's probe source can be podCIDR vs node IP.
marcos: Custom pinned to ifindex. It was only matching UDP initially, but we added a generic AF_INET/AF_INET6 fallback; that probably grabbed some TCP SYN/SYN-ACKs when the kernel reordered softirqs. Reproducible locally with `curl --interface` failing intermittently.
ess: Immediate mitigation: disabled the XDP program on gpu-nodeset-4a/4b/4c and restarted kubelet on one node. Evictions stopped within ~30s after restart. So looks like kubelet healthcheck false-positive from packet drops at XDP layer.
alex: Confirmed on node-4a: after eBPF disabled, node condition cleared and pods were allowed to stay. But we can't just turn off eBPF cluster-wide.
cheng: Long-term options: 1) patch eBPF to whitelist kubelet ports (10250/10255) and kube-proxy IPs, 2) change kubelet `--node-ip` or health probe to use localhost to avoid external path, 3) tune kubelet `--eviction-pressure-transition-period` or health check intervals to be more forgiving.
lina: I prefer patching eBPF to whitelist kubelet ports + add explicit tests. Also consider kubelet config to bind health check to loopback so it never traverses the problematic path.
alex: I'll open a PR to eBPF repo to add explicit whitelist + e2e that simulates XDP drop. For immediate safety we can: increase `--node-status-update-frequency` and `--eviction-soft` thresholds, plus schedule a controlled canary where we re-enable XDP with the whitelist.
marcos: Filed a ticket with kernel vendor; they acknowledged an XDP race in some backports. We're still on 5.15 LTS but variant exists.
deploy-bot: Rollout note: disabling XDP on 3 GPU nodes reduces perimeter filtering; schedule canary patch with whitelist and monitor `kubelet_healthz` and `xdp_drop_count` metrics.
ess: Action items: alex -> incident postmortem; marcos -> eBPF whitelist PR + tests; cheng -> validate kubelet config changes in staging; lina -> schedule canary at 15:00 UTC. I'll add these to #incidents board.
alex: Also adding cost impact: evicted GPU pods caused some jobs to requeue in other regions, ~2.4 GPU-hours wasted so far. Will include in postmortem.
marcos: TL;DR: false-positive kubelet network checks caused by XDP/eBPF dropping probe packets (dual-stack / fallback rule edge case). Fix: whitelist kubelet, adjust probe path, add monitoring for XDP drops.
lina: +1. I'll draft a short runbook step to disable eBPF safely in case of recurrence.
